_readme: Fills in synopsis/genre for high-value existing stubs, sourced from real fetched Gutenberg text. Skipped: Ulysses (Tennyson poem, not locatable on Gutenberg), Finnegans Wake (not on Gutenberg, in copyright), The Magic Mountain (only German original on Gutenberg, no English translation hosted).

books.title: Rip Van Winkle
books.author: Washington Irving
books.synopsis: A henpecked Dutch villager drinks with ghostly bowlers in the Catskill Mountains and wakes twenty years later to find his wife dead, his village transformed, and the American Revolution already history.

books.title: Essays
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.synopsis: Stevenson's personal essays roam from courtship and marriage to idling and old age, arguing for a life lived with zest and honesty rather than caution.

books.title: Essays
books.author: Francis Bacon
books.synopsis: Bacon's terse, aphoristic essays dispense worldly counsel on truth, ambition, love, and statecraft, seasoning practical wisdom with quotations from classical authors.

books.title: King John
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: King John schemes to hold his crown against a French-backed rival claimant and the Pope's excommunication, and orders his young nephew Arthur's death to secure it, unraveling his own reign in guilt and rebellion.

books.title: Henry IV
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: King Henry IV faces a rebel coalition while his wayward son Prince Hal carouses with the disreputable Falstaff, until Hal redeems himself by defeating the rebel Hotspur in single combat.

books.title: Phèdre
books.author: Jean Racine
books.synopsis: Queen Phaedra, consumed by an incestuous passion for her stepson Hippolytus, falsely accuses him of assaulting her once her husband Theseus returns, destroying them both.

books.title: The Golden Bough
books.author: James George Frazer
books.synopsis: Frazer surveys myth, magic, and ritual across cultures and history, tracing the priest-king of Nemi's sacred grove out into a vast comparative theory of how religion evolves from magic toward science.

books.title: The Anatomy of Melancholy
books.author: Robert Burton
books.synopsis: Burton anatomizes melancholy in exhaustive, digressive detail — its causes, symptoms, and cures — folding centuries of classical and contemporary learning into a work as strange as it is scholarly.

books.title: Sleeping Beauty
books.author: Anonymous
books.synopsis: A princess cursed at birth to die by a spindle is doomed instead to a hundred-year sleep, waking only when a prince's arrival finally breaches the thorned wood grown up around her castle.

books.title: Richard II
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: King Richard II seizes the banished Bolingbroke's inheritance, driving him to return with an army, depose Richard, and take the crown himself, leaving Richard to a prison cell and murder.

books.title: Troilus and Cressida
books.author: William Shakespeare
books.synopsis: Amid the endless siege of Troy, the lovers Troilus and Cressida pledge fidelity only for Cressida to be traded to the Greek camp and drift to a new lover, while Achilles sulks and Hector falls.

books.title: Metamorphoses
books.author: Ovid
books.synopsis: Ovid strings together the mythology of transformation, from the world's creation through Jove's loves, Actaeon's death, and Daedalus's flight, in a sprawling verse chain of gods and mortals remade.

books.title: Confessions
books.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
books.synopsis: Rousseau bares his own life without flattery, from a stolen ribbon in his youth to his scandalous loves and quarrels, in a founding work of unguarded autobiographical confession.

books.title: Poetics
books.author: Aristotle
books.synopsis: Aristotle dissects tragedy and epic poetry into their working parts — plot, character, and catharsis — grounding his theory in close readings of Homer and Sophocles.

books.title: In Search of Lost Time
books.author: Marcel Proust
books.synopsis: Proust's seven-volume novel follows an unnamed narrator's involuntary memories — most famously a madeleine dipped in tea — through the loves, society, and art of belle-époque and wartime France.
